newsitem.title: CROATIA: PRESS DIGEST - Croatia weekly - July 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Croatia weekly - July 9.

text.p: Following are the main stories from Croatian weekly news magazine Globus. Reuters has not verified the stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Perica Martinovic, head of the organised crime unit of Zagreb police, is fired after the murder of Spejtim Taci.
- Croatian Catholics will have to pay tax to the Church, says new Archbishop of Zagreb Josip Bozanic.

- Ivic Pasalic, President Tudjman's adviser for internal policy, comments on the current political situation in Croatia in an interview. Zlatko Canjuga is not the only one who should be credited for our election success: It was most of all the success of President Tudjman, Pasalic says.
- Private entrepreneur Ivica Todoric has an ambition to completely take over Zagreb's Hotel Intercontinental in which he already has a 49 percent stake.

- Mate Boban (1940-1997) - Death of a man who lost a state. The entire Herzegovina mourns Boban, while the top level of Croatian government ignores his death. Commentary: Is Mate Boban the first victim of the Hague tribunal?
- Murder of a pregnant woman will be punished with a 40-year prison sentence according to the proposed new penal code.
- Martin Katicic, former president of Privredna Banka, is pushing out the current county prefect Djuro Brodarac and taking over economic power in the Sisak-Moslavina county.

- Analysis of the Croatian political scene: Wastelands of Croatian democracy -- fractional struggle within HSLS, Budisa's fraction emerging as stronger. As many as 41 percent of HSLS voters support a coalition with HDZ and 50 percent believe Zagreb should be ruled by a coalition of the largest parties.
